name: Graph Inference Pipeline
description: Infer a graph structure from multivariate observations. Preprocess signals, compute pairwise scores between all variable pairs, then construct the graph via thresholding or optimization. The connectomics solution is the canonical example: preprocess calcium signals, compute partial correlations, threshold to produce a connectivity graph. Also covers causal graph discovery and correlation network inference.
applicable_when: Input is multivariate time series or paired observations
Goal is to infer a graph/network structure between variables
Pairwise scoring is the core operation
relationship_to_tabular: Structurally different from the tabular pipeline. There is no train/test split — all data is used to infer the graph. The 'model' is the scoring function, not a learned classifier.

nodes.name: preprocess_signals
nodes.description: Domain-specific signal preprocessing. For calcium imaging: lowpass filtering, differencing, thresholding, burst deconfounding. For time series: detrending, normalization, bandpass filtering.

nodes.name: compute_pairwise_scores
nodes.description: Compute a score for each pair of variables. For graph inference, this is typically partial correlation (via precision matrix), mutual information, or HSIC. For causal discovery, this uses the asymmetric feature primitives (IGCI, conditional entropy variance, etc.).
expansion_points: threshold_sweep_ensemble: average over dense grid of thresholds instead of selecting one
Can be replaced with learned pairwise scoring (GNN, attention)

nodes.name: apply_directionality
nodes.description: Optional: convert symmetric pairwise scores to directed edges. For causal inference, this uses the asymmetric feature difference pattern (f(X→Y) - f(Y→X)). For connectomics, this uses temporal precedence counting.

nodes.name: threshold_and_construct
nodes.description: Convert pairwise scores to a graph by thresholding, ranking, or optimization. The threshold can be fixed, adaptive (Bayesian), or swept and ensembled.

nodes.name: output_graph
nodes.description: Format the inferred graph as an adjacency matrix, edge list, or domain-specific format
